principle: This project is not debugged repeatedly. It is learned once and reused forever.

architecture_constraints.rule: Normal post list, category, tag, archive, and post detail data should flow through src/services/core and feature services.
architecture_constraints.reason: Bypassing the service layer fragments taxonomy, sorting, URL generation, and UI metadata behavior.

architecture_constraints.rule: When splitting large route, layout, or component files, put page logic, data adaptation, config normalization, static path builders, and page-level view models in src/services/; keep src/pages thin and extracted page components mostly presentational.
architecture_constraints.reason: The project already separates routing, page logic, and rendering; preserving this boundary prevents large files from reappearing under different names.

architecture_constraints.rule: Browser-only runtime interaction state such as DOM listeners, audio playback, pointer events, localStorage UI state, and Svelte runtime stores should live beside the owning component or feature, not in src/services/.
architecture_constraints.reason: src/services is for build-time/page-level logic and view models, while client interaction code is feature-local runtime behavior.

architecture_constraints.rule: Use getContentStore() for normal post index access. Keep RawPost, Markdown bodies, rendered HTML, passwords, and detail-only frontmatter behind the post-detail build-time service boundary; Feed must consume only body-free PostIndexEntry values.
architecture_constraints.reason: ContentStore is a lightweight, shared index; retaining or exposing raw entries recreates memory pressure and boundary leaks, while summary-only Feed output does not require raw content.

architecture_constraints.rule: Treat src/config.ts as owner-specific site configuration, not upstream defaults.
architecture_constraints.reason: This fork intentionally contains private layout, feature, and service choices.

known_failures.description: Chromium can be unable to launch inside the Codex macOS sandbox because Mach port rendezvous permission is blocked.
symptoms: Playwright Chromium launch fails before navigation
MachPortRendezvousServer Permission denied (1100)
browser process exits with SIGTRAP in the sandbox
solutions: run the selected Playwright command in host Terminal through Computer Use when available
run automated browser validation in CI
ask the user to run the exact selected Playwright command in a normal host Terminal when no external tool is available
do not use in-app Browser solely because Playwright failed to launch
do not fall back to agent-controlled Chrome

validation_truthfulness.rule: Do not claim that a command passed unless it actually ran and returned success in this workspace.
validation_truthfulness.failure_preflight_rule: If a package manager fails before invoking a target script, report package-manager preflight failure separately from script validation.
